title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
description: Ten documented Hendrix study settings, from collaborative rooms and computer labs to a fireplace library and senior research workspace.

cards.title: Build the Group Outline Here
cards.subtitle: Open collaborative study space in Bailey Library
cards.notes: Bring a group project and use the tables, whiteboards, comfortable seating, and projection capability to organize the work visually.
cards.short_summary: A flexible first-floor setting for collaborative writing, research, and peer-supported coursework.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix describes the Learning Commons as an open space with tables, comfortable seating, whiteboards, and computer projection capabilities.
cards.access_notes: Available during Bailey Library hours; scheduled peer-learning sessions and library programs may use the space.

cards.title: Work Through the Problem Set
cards.subtitle: Named peer-learning room inside Bailey Library
cards.notes: Bring chemistry notes and practice problems; check the current Peer Learning schedule before relying on an associate being present.
cards.short_summary: A defined library room used for scheduled general and organic chemistry peer learning.
cards.evidence_claim: The Spring 2026 Peer Learning schedule places General Chemistry and Organic Chemistry sessions in the Bailey Library Reading Room.
cards.access_notes: Located within Bailey Library and subject to library access; peer-learning support follows the posted semester schedule.

cards.title: Talk the Concept Through
cards.subtitle: Seminar setting used for physics peer learning
cards.notes: Use the seminar layout for discussion-based review, and bring specific physics questions during a posted Peer Learning session.
cards.short_summary: A structured discussion room suited to collaborative review and scheduled physics assistance.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix lists Physics Peer Learning in the Bailey Library Seminar Room on five evenings in its Spring 2026 schedule.
cards.access_notes: Located within Bailey Library; scheduled physics sessions follow the current Peer Learning calendar and library access rules.

cards.title: Settle In for a Digital Work Session
cards.subtitle: Around-the-clock computer lab beside Bailey Library
cards.notes: Choose this lab when an assignment needs a campus computer or printer; save work before the documented daily 5 a.m. restart.
cards.short_summary: A computer-equipped study option with semester-long 24/7 access and an on-site printer.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix identifies the Snoddy Computer Lab in Bailey Library as a 24/7 lab with one printer when residence halls are officially open.
cards.access_notes: Open 24/7 while residence halls are officially open; otherwise limited to regular library hours. Computers restart daily at 5 a.m.

cards.title: Give One Assignment Your Full Screen
cards.subtitle: Individual carrels in the Snoddy Academic Resource Center
cards.notes: Take a carrel when you want a defined personal workspace, and confirm semester access before planning an overnight study block.
cards.short_summary: Individual workstations in the academic resource center adjacent to Bailey Library.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix states that the Snoddy Academic Resource Center houses study carrels and is adjacent to Bailey Library.
cards.access_notes: Snoddy's Acxiom Computer Lab and Bailey Seminar Classroom have 24-hour semester access; the official page does not separately state carrel access.

cards.title: Put the Whole Team Around One Table
cards.subtitle: Seven group rooms on Bailey Library’s second floor
cards.notes: Head upstairs with your discussion agenda and ask library staff about current room-use procedures before beginning a long session.
cards.short_summary: A seven-room cluster intended for students who need an enclosed collaborative setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix states that Bailey Library's second floor contains seven group study rooms.
cards.access_notes: On Bailey Library's second floor and available only while the library is open; the official page does not state a reservation policy.

cards.title: Keep the Thesis Materials Together
cards.subtitle: Second-floor rotunda workspace for senior researchers
cards.notes: Make a librarian research appointment before requesting storage, then check out every library book before placing it in the cabinet.
cards.short_summary: A thesis-focused space where eligible seniors can keep checked-out research materials in locked storage.
cards.evidence_claim: Bailey Library provides seniors working on a thesis or project with a locked cabinet and shelving in the second-floor rotunda after a librarian appointment.
cards.access_notes: Restricted to seniors working on a thesis or project who have completed a research appointment with a librarian; keys must be checked out.

cards.title: Read Beside the Fireplace
cards.subtitle: Literature-and-language library in the Murphy House
cards.notes: Bring close reading or drafting work to the fireplace library, and check with Murphy staff when programs affect building access.
cards.short_summary: A cozy, book-lined alternative documented as a place where Hendrix students study beside the fireplace.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix says students study next to the fireplace in the first-floor library of the Bertie Wilson Murphy Building.
cards.access_notes: The official location page documents student use but does not publish daily access hours; confirm availability with Murphy Foundation staff.

cards.title: Rehearse the Presentation With the Tech
cards.subtitle: Interactive group-work suite in the SLTC
cards.notes: Use the seminar-style classroom to practice a presentation or develop media, and confirm availability before gathering a group.
cards.short_summary: A technology-centered group setting designed for presentations, video work, and interactive projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix describes the SLTC's Educational Technology Center as designed for interactive group work, with workstations and a seminar-style classroom for practicing presentations.
cards.access_notes: The official facilities page does not provide current open hours or a reservation process; verify access before planning a session.

cards.title: Print Before the Deadline
cards.subtitle: Computer lab in the Mills Center for Social Sciences
cards.notes: Use Mills 104C when you need a networked computer and printer, and arrange approved card access if work will extend beyond normal hours.
cards.short_summary: A named computer-and-printing workspace with published daytime access and an off-hours card option.
cards.evidence_claim: Hendrix lists Mills Lab in room 104C with networked computers, one printer, and published access from 8 a.m. to 10 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Published hours are 8 a.m.–10 p.m.; the lab may also be available during normal building hours or with approved card access after hours.

warnings: Current official pages do not publish standalone access hours or reservation rules for every room; affected cards explicitly direct students to verify availability.
